subproblem.title: Jacobi's formula: det on L(ℝⁿ) is C¹ with D det(T)[H] = det T · trace(T⁻¹H) at units
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, the determinant det : L(ℝⁿ) → ℝ, T ↦ T.det (ContinuousLinearMap.det), is C¹, and for every unit T of the ring L(ℝⁿ) (multiplication = composition) and every H ∈ L(ℝⁿ), D det(T)[H] = det T · trace(T⁻¹ ∘ H), where T⁻¹ := Ring.inverse T and trace is the trace of endomorphisms of ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun T : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn n ↦ T.det) ∧ ∀ T H : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn n, IsUnit T → fderiv ℝ (fun T : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn n ↦ T.det) T H = T.det * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn n) (Ring.inverse T ∘L H).toLinearMap
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). Every lemma cited below resolves after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` (checked with #check).

Setting. Fix n. Let b := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, the standard basis of ℝⁿ, and for T ∈ L(ℝⁿ) let [T] := LinearMap.toMatrix b b T (the matrix of T), whose (i, j) entry is the i-th coordinate of T(e_j).
1. (det is a polynomial in matrix entries.) For every T ∈ L(ℝⁿ), T.det = LinearMap.det T = Matrix.det [T] (LinearMap.det_toMatrix), and Matrix.det M = Σ_{σ ∈ Perm (Fin n)} sign σ • Π_i M (σ i) i (Matrix.det_apply).
2. (det is C¹; first conjunct.) For fixed i, j the map T ↦ [T] i j = (T e_j) i is a continuous linear functional on L(ℝⁿ) (evaluation at e_j, a continuous linear map L(ℝⁿ) → ℝⁿ, followed by the i-th coordinate, a continuous linear functional), hence C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff). Finite products and finite sums of C^∞ real functions are C^∞ (contDiff_prod, ContDiff.sum); the sign factor acts through ℤˣ, so rewrite sign σ • r = ((sign σ : ℤ) : ℝ) * r (Units.smul_def, zsmul_eq_mul) and use contDiff_const.mul. By step 1, T ↦ T.det is C^∞, in particular C¹ and differentiable at every T; so HasFDerivAt det (fderiv ℝ det T) T for all T.
3. (Factorization at a unit.) Let T be a unit, H ∈ L(ℝⁿ), K := Ring.inverse T ∘L H. Since T ∘L Ring.inverse T = 1 (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel), for every t ∈ ℝ: T + t • H = T ∘L (1 + t • K). By multiplicativity of the determinant (LinearMap.det_comp), det(T + t • H) = det T · det(1 + t • K).
4. (Second-order expansion.) [1 + t • K] = 1 + t • [K] (LinearMap.toMatrix_one, linearity of toMatrix), so by step 1 and Matrix.det_one_add_smul, det(1 + t • K) = Matrix.det(1 + t • [K]) = 1 + Matrix.trace [K] · t + p(t) · t², where p(t) := ((Matrix.det (1 + (X : ℝ[X]) • [K].map C)).divX.divX).eval t is a polynomial function of t. Moreover Matrix.trace [K] = trace K (LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace).
5. (Derivative along the line.) Put φ(t) := det(T + t • H) = det T · (1 + trace K · t + p(t) t²) (steps 3–4). The polynomial function t ↦ p(t) t² has derivative p′(t) t² + 2 t p(t), which is 0 at t = 0; hence φ has derivative det T · trace K at t = 0.
6. (Identification with the Fréchet derivative.) The curve γ(t) := T + t • H has derivative H at t = 0 and γ(0) = T; since det is differentiable at T (step 2), the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) gives that φ = det ∘ γ has derivative fderiv ℝ det T H at t = 0. By uniqueness of derivatives (HasDerivAt.unique) and step 5, fderiv ℝ (fun T ↦ T.det) T H = T.det * trace(Ring.inverse T ∘L H), the second conjunct. (For n = 0, L(ℝ⁰) is the zero ring, det ≡ 1 and every trace vanishes; the argument covers this case.) ∎

At a unit T: T + tH = T ∘ (1 + tK), K = T⁻¹H, so det(T + tH) = det T · det(1 + tK).
Matrix.det_one_add_smul: det(1 + tK) = 1 + t trace K + p(t) t², so d/dt|₀ det(T + tH) = det T · trace K.

subproblem.title: Gram operator of an injective linear map and the range projection A(A*A)⁻¹A*
subproblem.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ, every submodule K of ℝᴺ and every injective continuous linear map A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ with K = range A (ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)): the Gram operator G := A* ∘ A (A* = ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A) is a unit of the ring ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ (multiplication = composition); G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G is symmetric, ⟨G⁻¹v, w⟩ = ⟨v, G⁻¹w⟩ for all v, w ∈ ℝⁿ; and the orthogonal projection of ℝᴺ onto K is K.starProjection = A ∘ G⁻¹ ∘ A*.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (K : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), Function.Injective A → K = LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → IsUnit (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A) ∧ (∀ v w : Rn n, inner ℝ (Ring.inverse (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A) v) w = inner ℝ v (Ring.inverse (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A) w)) ∧ K.starProjection = A ∘L Ring.inverse (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A) ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). Every lemma cited below resolves after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` (checked with #check).
Source: parent proof, Setting and step 2 (P_{ψ(x)} = A G⁻¹ A*), specialized to an arbitrary injective A.
Setting. Fix n, N, K and A with A injective and K = range A (= LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap). K is finite-dimensional, so it has an orthogonal projection P := K.starProjection, with P z ∈ K (Submodule.starProjection_apply_mem) and z − P z ∈ Kᗮ (Submodule.sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal) for every z ∈ ℝᴺ.
1. (G is symmetric.) For v, w ∈ ℝⁿ: ⟨G v, w⟩ = ⟨A*(A v), w⟩ = ⟨A v, A w⟩ and ⟨v, G w⟩ = ⟨v, A*(A w)⟩ = ⟨A v, A w⟩. Hence ⟨G v, w⟩ = ⟨v, G w⟩.
2. (G is injective.) If G c = 0, then 0 = ⟨G c, c⟩ = ⟨A c, A c⟩ = ‖A c‖², so A c = 0, and c = 0 because A is injective.
3. (First conjunct: G is a unit of L(ℝⁿ).) By step 2 the kernel of the linear map G is ⊥, so G is a unit of the ring of linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ (LinearMap.isUnit_iff_ker_eq_bot) and hence det G ≠ 0 (LinearMap.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det). Then e := ContinuousLinearMap.toContinuousLinearEquivOfDetNeZero G is a continuous linear equivalence with underlying map G, and its inverse e.symm ∈ L(ℝⁿ) satisfies G ∘L e.symm = 1 = e.symm ∘L G (e.apply_symm_apply, e.symm_apply_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.ext). So IsUnit G in L(ℝⁿ). (For n = 0, L(ℝ⁰) is the zero ring and the argument still applies.) Consequently G ∘L G⁻¹ = 1 and G⁻¹ ∘L G = 1 (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel, Ring.inverse_mul_cancel).
4. (Second conjunct: G⁻¹ is symmetric.) For v, w ∈ ℝⁿ, using G(G⁻¹w) = w, step 1 and G(G⁻¹v) = v: ⟨G⁻¹v, w⟩ = ⟨G⁻¹v, G(G⁻¹w)⟩ = ⟨G(G⁻¹v), G⁻¹w⟩ = ⟨v, G⁻¹w⟩.
5. (Q := A ∘L G⁻¹ ∘L A* is the identity on K.) If z ∈ K = range A, write z = A c; then Q z = A(G⁻¹(A*(A c))) = A(G⁻¹(G c)) = A c = z.
6. (Q vanishes on Kᗮ.) If z ∈ Kᗮ, then for every c ∈ ℝⁿ, ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ = 0 since A c ∈ K. With c := A* z this gives ‖A* z‖² = 0, so A* z = 0 and Q z = A(G⁻¹ 0) = 0.
7. (Third conjunct: K.starProjection = Q.) For any z ∈ ℝᴺ, P z ∈ K and z − P z ∈ Kᗮ, so by linearity of Q and steps 5–6, Q z = Q(P z) + Q(z − P z) = P z + 0 = P z. As z is arbitrary, K.starProjection = Q = A ∘L Ring.inverse (A* ∘L A) ∘L A* (ContinuousLinearMap.ext). Equivalently: Q z ∈ K (it lies in range A) and z − Q z ⊥ K, because ⟨z − Q z, A c⟩ = ⟨A* z − A*(A(G⁻¹(A* z))), c⟩ = ⟨A* z − G(G⁻¹(A* z)), c⟩ = 0; so Q z = P z by Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero.
Steps 3, 4 and 7 are the three conjuncts. ∎

ker G = ⊥ ⇒ det G ≠ 0 ⇒ toContinuousLinearEquivOfDetNeZero gives a two-sided inverse in L(ℝⁿ), so IsUnit G and G G⁻¹ = G⁻¹ G = 1.
⟨G⁻¹v, w⟩ = ⟨G⁻¹v, G G⁻¹w⟩ = ⟨G G⁻¹v, G⁻¹w⟩ = ⟨v, G⁻¹w⟩.
Q = A G⁻¹ A* fixes K = range A and kills Kᗮ (A*z = 0 there); z = Pz + (z − Pz) gives K.starProjection = Q.

subproblem.title: Symmetry of the second derivative of a C² map on an open set (Schwarz)

Notation. ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). subproblem.title: Mean curvature through an injective parametrization differential
subproblem.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝᴺ, y ∈ ℝᴺ, every injective continuous linear map A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ with tangentSpace M y = range A, and every continuous linear S : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) (a bilinear map (a, b) ↦ S a b, not assumed symmetric) such that secondFundamentalForm M y (A a) (A b) = normalPart M y (S a b) for all a, b ∈ ℝⁿ: meanCurvature M y = normalPart M y (Σ_{l ∈ Fin n} S e_l (G⁻¹ e_l)), where e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 is the standard basis of ℝⁿ and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse (A* ∘ A), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M : Set (Rn N)) (y : Rn N) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N) (S : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), Function.Injective A → tangentSpace M y = LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap → (∀ a b : Rn n, secondFundamentalForm M y (A a) (A b) = normalPart M y (S a b)) → meanCurvature M y = normalPart M y (∑ l : Fin n, S (EuclideanSpace.single l 1) (Ring.inverse (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A) (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))

Notation. ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). Every lemma cited below resolves after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` (checked with #check).
Source: parent proof, step 8 (H(y) = (Σ_i S(a_i, a_i))^⊥ = (Σ_{k,l} g^{kl} S(e_k, e_l))^⊥), with the sibling sff_chart conclusion taken as the hypothesis hB.
Setting. T := tangentSpace M y = range A; hB: secondFundamentalForm M y (A a) (A b) = normalPart M y (S a b) for all a, b.
1. (Gram facts.) By the sibling gram_projection (K := T), G is a unit, so G(G⁻¹w) = w for all w (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel); and ⟨G v, w⟩ = ⟨A v, A w⟩ = ⟨v, G w⟩ for all v, w (adjoint identities).
2. (Frame.) Let b := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ T, indexed by ι := Fin (finrank ℝ T), and τ_i := (b i : ℝᴺ) = tangentFrame M y i. By definition meanCurvature M y = Σ_i secondFundamentalForm M y τ_i τ_i.
3. (Preimages.) Each τ_i lies in T = range A; choose a_i ∈ ℝⁿ with A a_i = τ_i.
4. (Normal part of a sum.) By hB, secondFundamentalForm M y τ_i τ_i = secondFundamentalForm M y (A a_i) (A a_i) = normalPart M y (S a_i a_i). Since normalPart M y v = v − tangentProjection M y v with tangentProjection M y linear, v ↦ normalPart M y v commutes with finite sums (map_sum, Finset.sum_sub_distrib). Hence meanCurvature M y = normalPart M y (Σ_i S a_i a_i).
5. (Reproducing formula.) For every c ∈ ℝⁿ: c = Σ_i ⟨A a_i, A c⟩ a_i. Indeed A c ∈ T; expanding the element ⟨A c, _⟩ of T in the orthonormal basis b (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr') and coercing to ℝᴺ (Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul, Submodule.coe_inner): A c = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, A c⟩ τ_i = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, A c⟩ A a_i = A(Σ_i ⟨τ_i, A c⟩ a_i); since A is injective, c = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, A c⟩ a_i = Σ_i ⟨A a_i, A c⟩ a_i.
6. (Expansion of G⁻¹ e_l.) Apply step 5 with c := G⁻¹ e_l. Since ⟨A a_i, A(G⁻¹e_l)⟩ = ⟨a_i, A*(A(G⁻¹e_l))⟩ = ⟨a_i, G(G⁻¹e_l)⟩ = ⟨a_i, e_l⟩ (adjoint_inner_right, step 1), we get G⁻¹ e_l = Σ_i ⟨a_i, e_l⟩ a_i for every l ∈ Fin n.
7. (Change of summation.) Using step 6, linearity of S e_l, then linearity of S and of evaluation at a_i:
   Σ_l S e_l (G⁻¹e_l) = Σ_l Σ_i ⟨a_i, e_l⟩ S e_l a_i = Σ_i (S (Σ_l ⟨e_l, a_i⟩ e_l)) a_i = Σ_i S a_i a_i,
   where ⟨a_i, e_l⟩ = ⟨e_l, a_i⟩ (real_inner_comm) and Σ_l ⟨e_l, a_i⟩ e_l = a_i is the expansion of a_i in the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr', EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). Symmetry of S is not used.
8. (Conclusion.) By steps 4 and 7, meanCurvature M y = normalPart M y (Σ_l S e_l (G⁻¹ e_l)). (For n = 0, T = {0}, ι is empty and both sides equal normalPart M y 0 = 0; the argument above covers this case.) ∎

Bilinearity and Σ_l ⟨e_l, a_i⟩ e_l = a_i: Σ_l S e_l (G⁻¹e_l) = Σ_i S a_i a_i.

Setting. A(x) := fderiv ℝ ψ x, A(x)* := adjoint A(x), G(x) := A(x)* ∘L A(x) ∈ L(ℝⁿ), J := Chapter02.areaJacobianAt ψ; for fixed x put S_v := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x v ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G(x). 1. (J = √(det ∘ G).) For every x, J x = √(det G(x)) (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp), (J x)² = det G(x) (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_sq_eq_det_adjoint_comp) and J x ≥ 0 (Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_nonneg). So J = fun x ↦ √(det G(x)).
2. (Positivity and Gram facts on V.) A = fderiv ψ is C¹ on V; with the ℝ-linear adjoint adjR, G = A*A is C¹ and DG(x)[v] = A*S_v + S_v*A (fderiv_clm_comp).
det_jacobi + chain rule: D(det∘G)(x)[v] = det G · (trace(G⁻¹A*S_v) + trace(G⁻¹S_v*A)), and the basis-sum/cyclicity argument gives trace(G⁻¹S_v*A) = trace(G⁻¹A*S_v).

ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) = Rn d with the standard inner product ⟨·,·⟩; L(E, F) := E →L[ℝ] F and L(ℝⁿ) := ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, a ring whose multiplication is composition (f * g = f ∘L g holds by rfl) with identity 1; for A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, so ⟨A* z, c⟩ = ⟨z, A c⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) and ⟨c, A* z⟩ = ⟨A c, z⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right); G := A* ∘L A and G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G; trace means LinearMap.trace ℝ ℝⁿ applied to the underlying linear map (.toLinearMap); e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1 (l ∈ Fin n) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ (= EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ l). Every lemma cited below resolves after `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` (checked with #check).
Source: parent proof, steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 (differentiate u = A a + u^⊥ and A* u^⊥ = 0, apply G⁻¹A*, take traces).
Setting. For x′ ∈ ℝⁿ: A(x′) := fderiv ℝ ψ x′, G(x′) := A(x′)* ∘L A(x′), a(x′) := Ring.inverse G(x′) (A(x′)*(u x′)). Fix x ∈ V and abbreviate A := A(x), G⁻¹ := Ring.inverse G(x), S := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x (so S v ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ), S v c ∈ ℝᴺ), and p := u x − A(a x). Let adjR := (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (𝕜 := ℝ)).toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap, the adjoint as an ℝ-linear continuous map (adjR L = L* by rfl).
1. (Differentiability and symmetry.) V is a neighbourhood of x. fderiv ℝ ψ is C¹ on V (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen), so x′ ↦ A(x′) is differentiable at x with derivative S. u is C¹ on the open V, hence differentiable at x. By the sibling coefficient_regularity, a is C¹ on V, hence differentiable at x. By the sibling second_derivative_symm, S v c = S c v for all v, c ∈ ℝⁿ.
2. (A(x′)* annihilates the normal part on V.) For x′ ∈ V put P(x′) := u x′ − A(x′)(a x′) and Q(x′) := A(x′)*(P(x′)). By the sibling gram_projection, G(x′) is a unit, so A(x′)*(A(x′)(a x′)) = G(x′)(Ring.inverse G(x′) (A(x′)*(u x′))) = A(x′)*(u x′) (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel), i.e. Q(x′) = 0 for all x′ ∈ V. As V is a neighbourhood of x, Q =ᶠ[𝓝 x] 0, so DQ(x) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Note P(x) = p.
3. (Derivative of P.) By the product rule for evaluation (fderiv_clm_apply): D(x′ ↦ A(x′)(a x′))(x)[v] = A(Da(x)[v]) + S v (a x). Hence DP(x)[v] = Du(x)[v] − A(Da(x)[v]) − S v (a x).
4. (Derivative of Q.) x′ ↦ A(x′)* = adjR (A x′) has derivative adjR ∘L S at x, i.e. v ↦ (S v)*. By the product rule (fderiv_clm_apply), DQ(x)[v] = A*(DP(x)[v]) + (S v)* p. By step 2, A*(DP(x)[v]) = −(S v)* p for every v ∈ ℝⁿ.
5. (Key pointwise identity.) Apply G⁻¹A* to step 3, use G⁻¹(A*(A c)) = G⁻¹(G c) = c (Ring.inverse_mul_cancel) and step 4: for every v,
   G⁻¹A*(Du(x)[v]) = Da(x)[v] + G⁻¹A*(S v (a x)) − G⁻¹((S v)* p).
   By symmetry (step 1), S v (a x) = S (a x) v.
6. (Traces.) Compute each trace in the orthonormal basis (e_l) (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner) and use step 5 with v := e_l:
   trace(G⁻¹ ∘ A* ∘ Du(x)) = Σ_l ⟨e_l, Da(x) e_l⟩ + Σ_l ⟨e_l, G⁻¹A*(S (a x) e_l)⟩ − Σ_l ⟨e_l, G⁻¹((S e_l)* p)⟩
   = trace Da(x) + trace(G⁻¹ ∘ A* ∘ S(a x)) − Σ_l ⟨e_l, G⁻¹((S e_l)* p)⟩.
   For the last sum, symmetry of G⁻¹ (gram_projection) and ⟨c, L* z⟩ = ⟨L c, z⟩ (adjoint_inner_right) give ⟨e_l, G⁻¹((S e_l)* p)⟩ = ⟨G⁻¹e_l, (S e_l)* p⟩ = ⟨S e_l (G⁻¹e_l), p⟩ = ⟨p, S e_l (G⁻¹e_l)⟩, so the sum equals ⟨p, Σ_l S e_l (G⁻¹ e_l)⟩ (inner_sum).
7. (Conclusion.) Rearranging step 6 and inserting p = u x − A(a x), Du(x) = fderiv ℝ u x, Da(x) = fderiv ℝ a x and S(a x) = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ ψ) x (a x):
   trace Da(x) + trace(G⁻¹ ∘L A* ∘L S(a x)) = trace(G⁻¹ ∘L A* ∘L Du(x)) + ⟨u x − A(a x), Σ_l S e_l (G⁻¹ e_l)⟩,
   which is the asserted identity. (For n = 0 all traces and the sum vanish.) ∎
proof_key_steps: On V, A*(u − A a) = A*u − G G⁻¹A*u = 0 (gram_projection), so the derivative of x′ ↦ A(x′)*(u − Aa)(x′) vanishes at x.
Product rule: D(u − Aa)[v] = Du[v] − A Da[v] − S v a and A* D(u − Aa)[v] = −(S v)*(u − Aa).
Apply G⁻¹A* and use symmetry S v a = S a v (second_derivative_symm; a differentiable by coefficient_regularity): G⁻¹A*Du[v] = Da[v] + G⁻¹A*S(a) v − G⁻¹(S v)*(u − Aa).
Trace in the basis e_l, with G⁻¹ symmetric: the last term traces to ⟨u − Aa, Σ_l S e_l (G⁻¹e_l)⟩, giving the identity.
